newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas rises on cold forecast, NYMEX rally.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas rises on cold forecast, NYMEX rally.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were more than 10 cents higher Friday, as buyers prepared for the upcoming cold snap expected to land in the Midwest by Tuesday, sources said.
Gulf prices climbed more than 15 cents to the $3.60s early and mid-$3.50s late, still at least 20 cents under December's index levels.
Temperatures are forecast to dip to levels about 10 to 20 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal by Tuesday in the Midwest, with the coldest weather expected in the central plains.
As a result, prices on the Midcontinent pipes gained about 15 cents to the mid-to-high $3.40s.
The Chicago city-gate market was quoted in the $3.80-3.90 area.
Temperatures in the region are expected to remain below-normal through next week.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices were up more than 10 cents to the $3.34-3.40 range, as forecasters called for temperatures as low as 20 degrees below-normal to reach Texas on Tuesday.
Similarly at the southern California border, traders reported closing deals in the high-$3.50s to low-$3.60s, up more than 10 cents from Thursday.
Temperatures in the Southwest are forecast to remain normal to slightly above-normal this weekend and into early next week.
